subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Hunter <sam.hunter@acme-retail.com>, Priya Das <pri.das@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Sam / Priya 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned on pain, goals, and next steps. Please reply with any corrections or items to add.

Key pain points you described:
- Growing per-token costs and unpredictability with current OpenAI usage (heavy batching for customer-facing chat).
- Vendor lock-in concerns: difficulty bringing model variants on-prem and differences in API semantics across providers.
- Latency spikes during peak traffic windows and insufficient observability into token-level spend per route.

Current stack & usage:
- Production: primarily OpenAI (chat + embeddings) for search personalization and support routing; Anthropic used for a subset of intent classification tests.
- Traffic: ~1.2M tokens/day, peak spikes tied to campaign events; latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for chat single-turn.
- Infra: mixed cloud tenancy (GCP us-central primary), some internal teams evaluating VPC-only deployments for PII workloads.

Success criteria for migration (as discussed):
- Equivalent or better output quality for core flows (chat + reranking/search).
- Cost reduction target: 25–40% per-token economics at current mix.
- Predictable latency within current SLOs during peak.
- Ability to run in a VPC / private deployment for regulated customer workloads.

Compatibility considerations we'll evaluate:
- API parity & prompt/response shape (chat messages, function-calling hooks, streaming).
- Embedding vector format and dimension differences for search reindexing.
- Tokenization differences and any effect on billing or prompt truncation.
- Quantization/throughput tradeoffs for your model shortlist.

Initial model shortlist (open/compatible options to evaluate):
- Llama 2/3 family (Redwood-verified variants)
- Mistral / Mistral-instruct variants
- Falcon 180B/40B SFT variants for hallucination-prone tasks (as tests)
- Smaller embedding-specialized models (for cost-sensitive routes)

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline):
- Rishi: produce a short compatibility checklist (API parity, tokenization, embedding dims) and preliminary perf projection by Wed 7/1.
- Aditya: draft a proposed model-variant and quantization shortlist with expected cost deltas by Fri 7/3.
- Marissa (me): coordinate a 60-min technical deep-dive next week with your infra team to map VPC/on-prem constraints proposed windows: Tue 7/6 or Thu 7/8.
- Sam / Priya: share the security questionnaire and any data residency requirements (we received an example during the call).

Attachments: I'm attaching two stubs for context: acme-integration-diagram.pdf (we sketched current flow) and a security questionnaire template we typically use in these evaluations.

If that all looks right I'll lock in the deep-dive for Tue 7/6 10:00am PT.

Thanks 

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0139

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Marissa 

Thanks for the thorough recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications / asks from our side: 

1) Security & compliance: we need to validate SOC 2 coverage and evidence around key management (KMS/HSM) for the VPC/on-prem option. I'm attaching our security questionnaire - would you confirm what you can provide?
2) Embeddings: we run an existing vector index (512-d) and will need minimal drift during reindexing. Any model change that changes dim will require a migration plan.
3) Timeline: we're targeting a pilot (non-customer-facing) deployment by end of Q3 to validate cost and latency improvements.

We can do Tue 7/6 10:00am PT for the technical deep-dive - please send a calendar invite with dial-in and include any pre-read.

Thanks,
Sam
Director, Search & Personalization
Acme Retail

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Sam / Priya 

Appreciate the quick reply and the questionnaire - got it. Couple quick items before the deep-dive: 

- Rishi: we'll surface SOC 2 artifact list and KMS integration notes; I'll flag anything that requires redaction or a separate NDA.
- Aditya: please prepare a short note on tokenization differences (OpenAI vs Llama/Mistral/Falcon) and an example prompt-pair to test.
- For the embedding dim question: if your vector dim is fixed (512), we'll prioritize models / projection layers that can produce 512-d vectors or propose a lightweight projection/retraining path - will include that in the pre-read.

I've booked Tue 7/6 10:00am PT and sent a calendar invite (includes a short pre-read link): https://app.hubspot.com/meetings/acme/rdw-deep-dive-0706

Pre-read highlights attached: short compatibility checklist + model shortlist rationale.

Looking forward; we'll aim to have the checklist and cost deltas in your inbox before the meeting.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
